speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: All of us feel very strongly about the ills of remote gambling, both the law-and-order concerns, as well as the social concerns that arise from problem gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Like many people outside this House, many of us here may also have personal convictions, values and beliefs about gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We respect and understand those personal viewpoints, values and beliefs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But we have to look at the issue from the national viewpoint, understanding the realities, practicalities and challenges at hand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Act provides for a general prohibition on remote gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It criminalises the entire spectrum of remote gambling activities and puts in place a comprehensive set of website- and payment-blocking measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It also provides for a tightly controlled exempt operator regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: So, when the Act was introduced, that was the framework: prohibition with a tightly-controlled valve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: At this rate, the remote gambling market will double in size roughly every 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singapore is not immune from these global trends, given our high Internet and smartphone penetration rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If we look at IDA's data, in 2014, our mobile penetration rate was at a whopping 148%, compared to the global rate then at 93%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Likewise, the Internet penetration rate in Singapore was at 73%, versus a global average of 35%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since the RGA came into force, we have effected a general prohibition, with robust enforcement and comprehensive blocking measures, to stem the growth of remote gambling within Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Several hundred gambling websites, together with bank accounts and payments linked to remote gambling services, have been blocked.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These measures are necessary, but not sufficient, to protect Singaporeans from the harms of illegal remote gambling and problem gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The nature of the Internet is such that it is not possible to completely block access to illegal gambling websites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We would be mistaken to believe that illegal online gambling does not exist today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Determined gamblers can circumvent website-blocking measures by using virtual private networks (VPNs) or through proxy websites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since February 2015 to date, Police have arrested 	Page: 16 more than 120 persons for remote gambling activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Underground gambling poses serious law-and-order concerns, particularly because of its linkages with organised crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Secret societies are known to offer illegal 4D and other gambling products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Illegal bookies also engage in unlicensed moneylending and money laundering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Illegal remote gambling does not come with any social safeguards, as the Minister for Social and Family Development reiterated a number of times in his response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no expenditure limit, no prohibition on the use of credit cards, no monitoring of gambling behaviour and no help provided to ensure responsible gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Many underground gambling operations are related to international crime syndicates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, in the run-up to and during the recent Euro 2016 football championship, Police worked with foreign law enforcement agencies through Operation SOGA VI, which was an Interpol-led effort, to arrest persons involved in syndicated remote betting operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As part of that operation, the Singapore Police Force apprehended 39 suspects in Singapore, who dealt with S$2.5 million of bets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Taking a realistic and clear-minded approach, we have to recognise that a complete ban on remote gambling will drive demand underground and create larger incentives for criminal syndicates to target Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, the Remote Gambling Act provided for a tightly-controlled exempt operator regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The exemption regime complements our strategy of general prohibition and blocking measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Seen in totality, it is an entire ecosystem and framework of measures trying to reduce the problem of online problem gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: From our experience with the terrestrial gambling space, this has worked well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A number of other jurisdictions, such as Hong Kong and Norway, adopt a similar approach – allowing regulated operators to complement a general prohibition of remote gambling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, we are very careful with providing the exemption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have imposed strict qualifying criteria for the exemption certificate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The exempt operator has to be a not-for-profit entity that distributes monies to public, social or charitable purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Directors and key officers of the operator cannot have been convicted of offences that render them unfit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The operator must possess a consistent track record of compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have also restricted the betting products that the operators can offer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Betting products are limited to those currently available via terrestrial channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Casino-style games and poker will not be allowed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The exempt operator is also required to implement strict social safeguards, to minimise potential harm to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development had earlier elaborated on those social safeguards, in response to Mr Christopher de Souza's question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We do not think gambling should be a way to make a living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We conduct public education on the potential harm of gambling and we have social safeguards in 	Page: 17 place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will continue to enforce strongly against all underground gambling activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our approach towards gambling is somewhat similar to the approach in many countries when managing other vices, such as drinking and smoking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Although we discourage drinking and smoking, we do not have a complete ban.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Instead, we manage the potential harm through regulations and public education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some have compared gambling to drug abuse and say if we allow a safety valve for gambling, why not have a safety valve for drug taking or drug offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I believe they are asking a rhetorical question and conflating the way in which you tackle crime and the way in which societies manage vices that have been around for ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The magnitude of harm resulting from drug abuse is vastly different and much more severe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our regimes towards drug abuse and vices, such as gambling, are , therefore, different in complexion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To conclude, the reality is that illegal gambling exists today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We cannot wish away the presence of underground markets, where criminal activities abound and signs of problem gambling go undetected.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: From what I have heard on the ground, the Ministry has performed quite well in terms of measures, enforcements, such as the blocking of the remote gambling sites.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Under what circumstances would the Government consider a total ban?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She asked about mixed signals, when in 2014 remote gambling was banned and then now in 2016 remote gambling is allowed through the exempt operators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As both the Minister for Social and Family Development and I have reiterated, in 2014 when the Bill was passed through Parliament, it was made clear that the framework comprised a comprehensive blocking of illegal websites, advertising targeted at Singaporeans and payments related to online gambling, as well as a safety valve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It reflected the 	Page: 18 way in which the problem could be managed and had been managed in the terrestrial sphere.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We were very clear and upfront that this was the framework and this was the way to tackle the growth of online gambling back in 2014.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let us be clear that we understand and we share the concerns of the Member and others who have voiced concerns consistently over the years about problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do not promote and we do not encourage it amongst our people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we recognise gambling exists and people have very different viewpoints and values about gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some object to gambling, fundamentally and in principle; others think that responsible gambling is possible and there is some autonomy they want to exercise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have to be practical and recognise the realities when regulating and managing these vices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, with Internet access and smartphone penetration rates in Singapore being amongst the world's highest, the reality is that online gambling is available at people's fingertips, whether it is in your home, as Mr Png Eng Huat mentioned in 2014 in his speech, or in people's pockets because they have smartphones with them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Likewise, with VPN and other technology, punters and syndicates will continue to try to circumvent blocking and enforcement measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hope people do not take to remote gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The collective effort must be undertaken by the Government, NGOs and VWOs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Public education and awareness raising have to work together with deterrence and law enforcement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But if you ask if a total ban will mean absolutely no online illegal gambling whatsoever, I think the answer is no.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the Member has said earlier, in the last year plus, we had not had this exempt operator regime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the framework, there was, in fact, a grandfathering of existing remote betting facilities by both the applicants until the application is resolved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in some ways, it has not been an entire total ban, although we had implemented blocking measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, online gambling has been here for the last year plus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is attracting many people and is set to grow.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, estimates are that the global online gambling size was around US$40 billion last year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the last five years, it grew by 6% to 8% percent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will double every 10 years or so, assuming that the rate does not increase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And most of us are very connected to the Internet and are very tech-savvy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these global trends will impact us and we have to recognise that these trends will affect us.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, we have to make sure our system is sufficiently robust, sophisticated and practical to address them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They say, "There are global trends, we know all these but do you have any data?" I think Mr Christopher de Souza had also asked this question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the Minister for Social and Family Development had earlier alluded to, the nature of remote gambling, especially underground illegal gambling, is such that it is hard to get precise and accurate details of the nature and extent or the exact number of people who are accessing these sites.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a result, we can only rely on best estimates, where there will be varying figures, estimates and statistics.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2013, MHA, prior to introducing the Bill, had conducted and commissioned a study.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then-Second Minister for Home Affairs mentioned this in a speech in 2013.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This was a study by an external consultant for the Ministry which included a survey of Internet users.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That was 2013, so it is just one data point.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are varying estimates by external analysts on the size of remote gambling in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We can look for these reports, you can purchase them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The reports analyse the remote gambling market around the world, including in specific jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Police carried out more than 100 raids against illegal gambling – terrestrial and online – each year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2015, close to 300 people were arrested for illegal gambling, with about 50 charged under the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: About 90% of those arrested for illegal football gambling were involved in online football gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: More than one-third of those arrested for illegal lotteries were involved in online remote lotteries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Police also continue to arrest illegal bookmakers and agents on an on-going basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our experience with terrestrial gambling since the 1960s is that illegal terrestrial gambling activities have largely been kept under control, based on recent arrest figures, which number in the few hundreds each year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In a way, the safety valves in Singapore Pools and in Singapore Turf Club have partly contributed to that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have observed and monitored the illegal gambling situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Whilst the ban and the prohibitions have reduced traffic to a lot of these sites, there is still this traffic from Singapore to some of the blocked sites, via diversionary measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is also traffic to new sites, which pop up each and every day.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As part of implementing the exempt operator regime, MHA is working with both operators to conduct surveys and studies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, the experience of foreign jurisdictions with narrow exempt operator frameworks – Hong Kong and Norway – has allowed regulators and law enforcement agencies to collect data on betting patterns, which may otherwise have gone undetected.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This helps them to finetune policy decisions relating to remote gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I hope that this addresses the Member's question about what has been the experience since 2015 to date.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have given Members some data points and statistics.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the end of the day, given the nature of what we are grappling with, it is very difficult to have and to pin down the exact numbers as you would with something that happens legitimately on a daily basis out in the daylight.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That also answers the Member's third question, which is why not invest more in technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The exempt operator framework only provides for what is already existing in the terrestrial framework.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It does not provide for casino-style games and poker.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue and must continue to invest in technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But at the end of the day, we recognise that this is almost like a technological cat-and-mouse game and we recognise that there will still be growth in online 	Page: 20 gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We must have an entire ecosystem – prohibitions, enforcement, education, moral suasion, family support, community support as well as a tightly-controlled valve – that reflects what we do in the terrestrial sphere.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Could we also consider or are we considering monitoring at a more focused level whereby we gather data from the gambling accounts and ascertain gambling patterns for earlier counselling intervention?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The person can make an application but he has to turn up physically in person to be verified at one of the centres, to verify his age and eligibility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Two-factor authentication takes place through a mobile number, which ought to belong to the real gambler.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And there will be monitoring by the operators and regulators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If it is detected that an account is used as a proxy, then, the exempt operators would, first of all, have to take firm action.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Additionally, the regulators and the Police would have to see if any offence has been committed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, in both Hong Kong and Norway, the valve has enabled the regulators there to have more data points about online gambling trends.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can use this information to help sharpen, tighten and revise their overall framework on online gambling.
